name: Viyash Scientific Ltd
title: Viyash Scientific Ltd - 512529 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 EBITDA crossed INR200 crore (21.7% margin) on merger synergies, but capital-cycle signals are thin: no capacity cut, management plans R&D and capex build and quotes INR800 crore FY27/28 EBITDA-style targets loosely.

summary.headline: Viyash Q4 FY26 revenue INR920 crore (+19.1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA about INR200 crore at 21.7% margin; FY26 PAT INR225 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as the strongest quarter in company history, the first full 12-month results of the combined Viyash-SeQuent entity. Revenue rose 19.1% YoY to INR920 crore, with formulations up 28% to INR499 crore and APIs up 5% to about INR384 crore. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 64% to INR200 crore and PBT swung from a INR37 crore loss to a INR125 crore profit. FY26 revenue was INR3,420 crore (+13.8%), adjusted EBITDA INR702 crore (+59.6%), and PAT INR225 crore versus INR16 crore in FY25. Management also cited a credit rating upgrade to AA- (long-term) and A1+ (short-term).

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR37 crore PBT and loss of INR32 crore PAT in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR349 crore PBT / INR225 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT more than 26x; PAT more than 14x vs INR16 crore

segments.name: Animal Health formulations
segments.commentary: All regions growing strongly per management. Animal health business moved from a flat INR350 crore plus or minus INR10 crore over five years to a INR400 crore run rate this year. Companion animal platform build-out is planned for FY27 with a Boehringer Ingelheim distribution partnership.

segments.name: Human health formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 formulations up 28% YoY. Shift toward complex products and internalised APIs; a dedicated potent oncology lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next. US subsidiary (60% owned) revenue about INR400-425 crore.

segments.name: API and CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue up 8% to INR1,491 crore; Q4 API up 5%. Management deliberately cut low-margin intermediates. Life cycle management CDMO business with 8-10 innovators is about INR200-225 crore and is expected to grow about 40% in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 life cycle management (innovator) CDMO business expected to grow about 40% from a base of about INR200-225 crore.
Management expects comfortable double-digit API growth next year, roughly in line with formulations growth.
Management sees 15% annual growth as possible over the next five years; a detailed strategy and investor meeting are planned, possibly in June.
Revenue target of INR1,000 crore EBITDA stated, with timing to be confirmed at the investor meeting; management earlier cited INR800 crore for FY27 or FY28.
Synergies accrued at about INR50-60 crore annualised, with a target of INR125-150 crore annualised over the next 12-18 months.
Tax rate to be modelled at about 27% for FY27 and FY28, moving to 26-27% after one-off merger-related adjustments roll off.
Goodwill amortisation to fall to about INR35 crore in FY27 from about INR100 crore in FY26; depreciation excluding this to stay similar to FY26.
EBITDA margins expected to be maintained, but FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs.
Management is evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and options to buy out minority stakes (Spain option by 2028).
capex_capacity: Manufacturing expansion in Spain and debottlenecking at the Turkey manufacturing site are underway.
Capex approved for R&D expansion; companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x, targeting 7-8 products per year, with R&D hiring starting over the next six months.
Capex for capacity increase in Viyash has been invested and is awaiting approval, which management expects to bring further synergies.
Two high-potent dedicated API facilities; API batch capability ranges from 0.5-1 kg up to 100 kg.
API R&D team of about 250 scientists including analytical and process; human health formulation R&D about 55-60 scientists.
demand_pricing: Animal health: about 70-80% of API volumes go to innovators; generics pricing falls to about 60-70% of innovator price versus 10-15% in human generics.
Companion animal addressable market in Europe about $1 billion (excluding vaccines); India companion animal market a few hundred crore.
Formulation model is partnership-based, with development paid by partners and profit share typically 50:50 (customers cited include Cipla and Dr. Reddy's).

Raw material and freight: impact in March was immaterial; freight added INR1-2 crore in Q4; solvent costs were the main pressure. Price increases are being used to offset, with key materials stocked for 1-2 quarters.
Commodity intermediate margins are about 30-35%; management is exiting these in favour of APIs and formulations.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the CDMO business and how will it scale over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the life cycle management CDMO business is about INR200 crore with 8-10 big innovators, and 90%-plus of relationships are existing. Ramp-up of NCE Phase III CDMO work takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Which subsidiaries drive minority interest, and how big are they?
qa_highlights.answer: Viyash owns 60% of the US formulations business (revenue about INR400-425 crore) and 60% of the Spain business (FY26 revenue about INR550 crore). Minorities account for about 20% of PAT; Spain buy-back option exists by 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Animal health growth priorities and Boehringer Ingelheim partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on API for patent expiries from 2028 onwards (15-20 products identified, 5-6 large), geography expansion for large animal products, and companion animals with the BI distribution deal and 7-8 new products per year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability versus pure-play API peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margins to hold at current levels, plus or minus 1-2%, through forward and backward integration and dropping commodity products. Margin gains beyond that are expected only with CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables growth and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose mostly with revenue; days increased by only about 5-6 days in Q4. Focus is on converting EBITDA into PAT, with a tax regime shift for some subsidiaries from 34-35% to 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and geopolitical impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact began in March and was not material; key materials are stocked for 1-2 quarters and price increases are being used to offset solvent and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is API growth single digit and when will it turn double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intermediates were cut deliberately; quality API and animal health APIs are growing double digit, and FY27 should see comfortable double-digit API growth with more approvals.

risks_watch: Investment year in FY27 (R&D, pre-operating costs) may dilute EBITDA margins despite management's margin-maintenance guidance.
Raw material cost volatility (solvents, freight) linked to geopolitical disruption; management says price increases can offset only for now.
Receivables growth outpacing revenue in some geographies (e.g. Turkey) with long credit periods; EBITDA-to-PAT conversion remains a stated focus.
Synergy realisation (INR50-60 crore run-rate versus INR125-150 crore target) depends on approvals taking 12-18 months.
US companion animal generic guidance is complex (BA/BE requirements), delaying the planned US entry.
Minority interest (about 20% of PAT) and the Spain buy-back timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and integration, with a clear focus on execution. Management was less precise on specific numbers (e.g. revising the INR1,000 crore EBITDA target timing and asking for later confirmation at an investor meeting), and it deferred detailed strategy until a planned June meeting.
key_quotes: Q4 FY '26 is the strongest quarter in the company history. EBITDA surpasses INR200 crores.
We are able to take it to INR400 crores run rate.
Whatever we are doing this year, I can expect next year at least 30%, 40% growing innovator business.
Yes, 15% definitely quite possible. Still, we are working on the detailed strategy.

adds.what: Manufacturing expansion in Spain and debottlenecking at Turkey manufacturing site (capacity figures not stated)
Capacity increase in Viyash: capex invested, awaiting approval
Dedicated potent oncology lab in R&D being readied (R&D, not production)

growth.why: Management expects comfortable double-digit API growth in FY27 (in line with formulations) and 40% growth in the ~INR200-225 crore LCM CDMO business, with 15% annual growth possible over five years; backing is partial, citing Spain/Turkey expansion, a pending Viyash capacity capex approval, and partner-led formulations, but no capacity sizes or timelines were given.
